edit_summary: Leave a failed appended certificate node linked in the caller's X.509 chain after freeing it on parse rollback.
root_cause: Appending a DER certificate to a nonempty chain temporarily links a new node; parse failure must detach that node before freeing it.
effect_path: A nonempty certificate chain appends crt->next, x509_crt_parse_der_core fails on the new DER, the failure path frees crt, and later mbedtls_x509_crt_free walks prev->next into the freed node.
guard_p1: The caller parses an invalid DER certificate into a chain that already contains a parsed certificate.
guard_p2: The same invalid DER as the first certificate has no previous chain link to retain the freed node; a valid appended DER is not freed on rollback.
hardness_reason: The allocation/link happens before deep DER parsing, while the stale traversal occurs later in the public chain destructor.
naturalness_reason: Forgetting to unlink a newly appended list node on parse rollback is a natural ownership-transfer bug in linked certificate chains.
explanation: Appending a DER certificate to a nonempty chain temporarily links a new node; parse failure must detach that node before freeing it. Without the detach, a later chain free traverses freed memory.
effect_site_expected: library/x509_crt.c:3208-3228 mbedtls_x509_crt_free traverses and frees cert_cur->next
conditional_expected: Positive input appends a malformed DER cert to a nonempty chain; negatives parse the malformed DER into an empty chain or append a valid DER cert.

edit_summary: Leave a freed PKCS7 signer issuer-name sublist reachable so outer parse cleanup traverses it again.
root_cause: pkcs7_free_signer_info must make the signer issuer-name list idempotently empty after freeing the ASN.1 name nodes.
effect_path: Malformed signed-data parsing calls pkcs7_free_signer_info during signers-set cleanup, then mbedtls_pkcs7_parse_der calls mbedtls_pkcs7_free on the same partially populated object; the second cleanup reads signer->issuer.next and walks freed issuer nodes.
guard_p1: A PKCS7 SignedData object has parsed at least one signer issuer name and then fails while parsing the signer-info set or a later signed-data field.
guard_p2: Malformed data that fails before issuer names are allocated, or a valid SignedData object, does not cause the two cleanup routes to traverse the same sublist.
hardness_reason: The first free is in a nested signers-set cleanup helper; the later use is in outer PKCS7 object teardown after parse error routing.
naturalness_reason: Making a sublist free helper idempotent by nulling the head is a realistic C cleanup invariant for partially parsed ASN.1 structures.
explanation: pkcs7_free_signer_info must make the signer issuer-name list idempotently empty after freeing the ASN.1 name nodes. Without that, a nested cleanup and the outer PKCS7 teardown can traverse the same freed list.
effect_site_expected: library/pkcs7.c:760-766 mbedtls_pkcs7_free invokes pkcs7_free_signer_info again and reads the stale issuer list
conditional_expected: Positive input reaches a parsed signer issuer sublist before a later PKCS7 parse failure; negatives fail before signer issuer allocation or complete parsing successfully.

edit_summary: Keep a freed DTLS retransmission flight list in handshake state after the incoming flight completes.
root_cause: The DTLS handshake flight list is owned by handshake state until an incoming flight makes the previous outbound retransmission list obsolete; that owner slot must be cleared after freeing the list.
effect_path: A DTLS handshake builds an outbound retransmission flight, receives the peer's next flight, mbedtls_ssl_recv_flight_completed frees handshake->flight, and later handshake teardown calls mbedtls_ssl_flight_free(handshake->flight) again.
guard_p1: The DTLS handshake has a nonempty retransmission flight and receives the last message of the peer's next incoming flight.
guard_p2: A TLS stream transport, or a DTLS state without a buffered outbound flight, does not leave a flight list to be freed twice.
hardness_reason: The first free occurs on a DTLS state transition; the second free occurs later in handshake teardown, separated by timer and buffering state cleanup.
naturalness_reason: DTLS retransmission queues are lifecycle-owned state, and clearing an obsolete queue after a flight transition is a natural minimal fix.
explanation: The DTLS handshake flight list is owned by handshake state until an incoming flight makes the previous outbound retransmission list obsolete. If the owner slot is not cleared, teardown can free the same flight list again.
conditional_expected: Positive flow is DTLS with a nonempty retransmission flight completed by a later incoming flight; negatives are stream TLS or DTLS states without a saved flight.

edit_summary: Leave a freed DTLS future-epoch record buffer reachable after it is loaded into the active input record.
root_cause: The DTLS future-record buffer is a one-shot handoff cache; after ssl_load_buffered_record consumes and frees it, the cache data pointer must be cleared.
effect_path: A DTLS record from the next epoch is buffered, later ssl_load_buffered_record copies it into ssl->in_hdr and calls ssl_free_buffered_record, and mbedtls_ssl_buffering_free or a later cleanup route calls ssl_free_buffered_record again on the stale data pointer.
guard_p1: The peer sends a valid next-epoch record while the current epoch is still active, causing future_record.data to be allocated.
guard_p2: No future-epoch record, or a buffered record whose epoch never becomes current before teardown, avoids the consume-then-free-again path.
hardness_reason: The first free happens in the buffered-record load path; the second is reached through generic DTLS buffering cleanup after handshake state advances.
naturalness_reason: One-shot buffering caches commonly require clearing the consumed data pointer, and this edit is a plausible missed handoff-state update.
explanation: The DTLS future-record buffer is a one-shot handoff cache. If the consume path frees the data but keeps the cache pointer, later generic buffering cleanup can free the same record buffer again.
conditional_expected: Positive flow buffers a next-epoch DTLS record and later loads it when the epoch changes; negatives do not buffer a future record or never consume it before cleanup.
